what_its_for: Naftifine is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal skin infections such as athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), and ringworm (tinea corporis). It works by stopping the growth of the fungus that is causing your infection.
how_to_take: Naftifine comes as a cream or gel that you apply directly to your skin. Wash and dry the affected area thoroughly before applying. Apply a thin layer of the medicine to the infected skin and the area around it. Rub it in gently. Wash your hands well after applying unless you are treating your hands. Do not get it in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not swallow it. Do not bandage or wrap the treated area too tightly unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: For the cream (1%): Apply once a day to the affected area. For the gel (1%): Apply once a day to the affected area. For the cream (2%): Apply once a day to the affected area. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Treatment usually lasts 2 to 4 weeks depending on the type of infection.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply naftifine, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store naftifine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep the tube or bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting naftifine in your eyes, nose, mouth, or vagina. Do not use it on broken, cut, or severely irritated skin unless directed by your doctor. Avoid tight-fitting clothing or shoes over treated areas, as this can slow healing. Do not share towels, clothing, or shoes with others while you have a fungal infection. Avoid using other skin products on the same area unless your doctor approves.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if your skin condition gets worse or does not improve after 4 weeks of treatment. Also contact your doctor if you notice severe redness, burning, blistering, swelling, or oozing at the application site. Call if you develop signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, dizziness, or trouble breathing. Let your doctor know if the infection spreads to other areas of your body.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within the first week of treatment. However, it is very important to keep using the medicine for the full amount of time prescribed by your doctor, even if you feel better sooner. Stopping too early may allow the fungus to grow back.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using naftifine. Use only if your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children under 12 years of age have not been fully established. Talk to your doctor before using in children. Older Adults: No special dose adjustments are typically needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's guidance.
